chunks: And al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

“The mustahadah performs ghusl at the time of salat al-zuhr, then performs the zuhr and 'asr prayers; then she performs ghusl at the time of al-maghrib, then performs the maghrib and 'isha' prayers; then she performs ghusl at the time of al-subh, then performs salat al-fajr. And there is no harm in her husband approaching her whenever he wishes, except during the days of her hayd, in which case her husband keeps away from her.”
And he said: “No woman ever did this seeking reward except that she was cured of that.”

key_terms.احْتِسَابًا: seeking divine reward and counting the act with Allah
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the time of the maghrib prayer
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istihadah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: she performs ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.حَيْضِهَا: her menstruation, during which special rulings apply
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: the time of the zuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for ghusl, prayer, and marital relations for a mustahadah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for the mustahadah regarding repeated ghusl tied to the prayer times of zuhr, maghrib, and subh, and clarifies that marital relations are permitted for her outside the days of hayd. It also mentions that a woman who consistently does this seeking divine reward is granted relief from that condition.
